sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northwest part of the Borough of Linden, between the Roselle township line at the top and Elm Street at the bottom, and from Lafayette Street on the west to the east side of Wood Avenue. St. George Avenue is drawn along the top of the sheet, with the Borough of Roselle beyond the dash-and-dot township line. Wood Avenue runs down the right-hand side, and the blocks east of it are numbered 4. The middle of the sheet is crossed by Gesner Street, Gibbons Street, a dash-and-dot Borough Line and Curtis Street, with Henry Street and Elm Street lower down. Ainsworth Street runs across the sheet, drawn with a jog near Curtis Street, and Summit Street, drawn slanting through the blocks at upper left, is turned a few degrees from the rest of the grid. The southwest quarter is a grid of Lafayette, Spruce, Miner Terrace and Brook Streets cut by Curtis, Henry and Elm; these blocks, numbered 17 to 25, are mostly cut into narrow vacant lots with a few frame dwellings. West Brook runs diagonally from the upper right to the bottom of the sheet, with a bridge at Gibbons Street. The built-up part is scattered small frame dwellings with private garages, a few stuccoed, and two blue-tinted buildings north of Gesner Street. Six-inch and ten-inch water pipes are marked in St. George Avenue, Wood Avenue, Gibbons Street, Ainsworth Street and some cross streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees, and a compass rose at the right edge points north to the upper right. Sheet 3 continues to the east and sheet 8 to the south.
notes: St. George Avenue is West Saint Georges Avenue today; Curtis, Henry, Gibbons and Elm are West Curtis Street, West Henry Street, West Gibbons Street and West Elm Street west of Wood Avenue.
Wood Avenue is North Wood Avenue in today's data.
Ainsworth Street jogs near Curtis Street, as it does in today's street data.
100 ft. St George Av, Ainsworth, Gesner, Summit, Wood Av, Lafayette area, brook; one part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of the Borough of Linden east of Wood Avenue, from the north side of Gibbon Street at the top to Blancke Street at the bottom, and from Wood Avenue on the left to Maple Avenue and Pratt Place on the right. Gibbon, Curtis, Henry and Elm Streets cross the sheet from side to side, with Washington Avenue running diagonally down through the middle and Moore, Coke, Conklin and Pratt Places crossing between Henry and Elm. A dash-and-dot Borough Line crosses the upper blocks between Gibbon and Curtis Streets. In the upper right the 1st and 2nd Avenues, Walnut Street and Maple Avenue are laid out in long diagonal blocks of narrow lots, numbered 25 to 27, with Union Avenue and Cleveland Avenue and the blocks east of Maple Avenue (numbers 28 to 30 and 42 to 43) cut off by the right edge. The large building at upper left is Linden Public School No. 1, with a hose house and fire department building of the Linden Hall volunteer company to its east. The Reformed Church stands on Wood Avenue, and Grace Episcopal Church and the Linden Club House on Elm Street and Luttgen Place; A. Braun's brass factory is shown between Elm Street and Blancke Street. Most of the other buildings are small frame dwellings, some stuccoed, with a few private garages. At the foot of the sheet Hussa Street and Blancke Street meet at a wedge-shaped junction with a pipe line. Monmouth Place is a short street in the lower right. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, the street grid is turned about 51 degrees on the page, and a compass rose and a graphic scale stand at the bottom.
notes: Gibbon is East Gibbons Street today; Curtis, Henry, Elm and Blancke are East Curtis Street, East Henry Street, East Elm Street and East Blancke Street east of Wood Avenue.
Wood Avenue is North Wood Avenue in today's data.
Luttgen Place and Monmouth Place are not in today's street data; the junction with Coke Place at Elm Street is not in today's data either, since Coke Place stops at Henry Street.
The Linden Public School here is No. 1; the school on sheet 4 is No. 5.
100 ft. Wood Av, Henry, Curtis, Gibbons, Elm, Monmouth Pl, Lutgen Pl, Blancke; one part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the northern corner of the Borough of Linden along the Roselle line, in the residential grid north of the Pennsylvania Railroad. It is bounded on the north by St. George Avenue, drawn along the township line with the Borough of Roselle beyond it, on the west by Clark Street and on the east by Lincoln Street, and runs south to Henry Street. The cross streets running parallel to St. George Avenue in the lower half of the sheet are Pierce Avenue, Van Buren Avenue, Jackson Avenue, Cleveland Avenue, Union Avenue, Curtis Street and Middlesex Street; Roselle Street, Bower Street and McCandless Street run across them. Short stubs of Chestnut, Victory, Cavell and Fern Streets and Home Terrace enter from the Roselle side, and Briant Place, 4th Avenue and 3rd Avenue appear at the western margin. The blocks are almost entirely laid out in building lots, most of them still vacant in 1920; the scattered houses are small frame dwellings, many marked stuccoed, with private garages and a few auto sheds. The one large building is Linden Public School No. 5, drawn from plans, a brick-faced hollow tile and reinforced concrete building on the block between Curtis Street and Middlesex Street east of Bower Street. A fire alarm box stands at Roselle Street and Cleveland Avenue, and water pipes are shown in St. George Avenue and Roselle Street. Block numbers run from 17 to 50 in the west and from 213 to 246 in the east. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 50 degrees to the page, and the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: St. George Avenue is East Saint Georges Avenue today; Curtis is East Curtis Street and Henry is East Henry Street.
Union Avenue has no junction with the cross streets in today's street data; it was not used for control.
Linden Public School No. 5 is drawn from plans.
100 ft. Clark, Roselle, Bower, McCandless, Lincoln x Pierce, Van Buren, Jackson, Cleveland, Union, Curtis, Middlesex, Henry; one part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5 covers the northern blocks of Linden on both sides of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad, from St. George Avenue on the Roselle line down to Blancke Street. Lincoln Street runs along the western margin, with the ends of Jackson and Cleveland Avenues beyond it; Carnegie Street, the two roadways of Baltimore Avenue either side of the B. and O. tracks, John, Charles, Paul and Peter Streets, Chandler Avenue and St. Marks Street run down the page. The cross streets are Union Avenue, Curtis, Middlesex, Henry, Passaic Avenue, Hackensack Avenue, Monmouth Avenue and Blancke; Linden Avenue, Morris, Frank and Rivington Streets enter from the Borough of Roselle across St. George Avenue. A brook runs beside Union Avenue in the northeast. Along St. George Avenue stand a row of small stores, among them a plumber, a tailor, a poolroom, a clothing store, a meat market, a second-hand furniture store, a hardware store, a dry goods and notions store, paints and glass, a tailor and furniture store and junk shops, with tenements and an ornamental iron works nearby. The rest of the part is laid out in narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, a bicycle shop at Chandler Avenue and Middlesex, a filling station on block 263, and the A.A.A. Congregation of Linden Synagogue on block 291 at Chandler Avenue. A large tract east of Paul Street and Union Avenue is undivided. Block numbers run from 228 to 292. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; two insets at 50 feet to an inch occupy the upper right and lower left corners of the sheet.
notes: St. George Avenue is East Saint Georges Avenue today; Curtis, Henry and Blancke are East Curtis Street, East Henry Street and East Blancke Street.
Paul Street and Hackensack Avenue are not in today's street data.
Baltimore Avenue is drawn as two roadways either side of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad; it was not used for control.
A.A.A. Congregation of Linden Synagogue on block 291.

sheet-6-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 6 covers the northeastern blocks of Linden along the Roselle line, east of the heavy dividing line that separates it from the Grasselli Park part of the same sheet. St. George Avenue runs along the top on the township line, with the Borough of Roselle beyond it, and Union Avenue runs diagonally below it beside a brook. Chandler Avenue, St. Marks Street and Cranford Avenue run down the page, crossed by Middlesex Street, Henry Street, Passaic Avenue, Hackensack Avenue, Monmouth Avenue, Blancke Street, Hussa Street and Bergen Avenue at the bottom. The blocks are divided into narrow lots and only lightly built up, with scattered frame and a few brick dwellings and private garages; a row of stores and dwellings, some of brick, faces St. George Avenue at Chandler Avenue, among them a harness shop and a hay and feed store. Public School No. 4, a brick and tile building with reinforced concrete floors in the corridors, stands on block 267 between Passaic and Hackensack Avenues at Cranford Avenue. Block 240, a large lot on St. George Avenue east of Cranford Avenue with an auto repair shop, sheds, a hotel and a buried gasoline tank, is marked 400 feet not in scale. East of Cranford Avenue blocks 299 and 340 are unplatted, and a brook crosses the lower right corner. A fire alarm box and water pipes of 6, 10 and 12 inches are shown. Block numbers run from 239 to 340. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: St. George Avenue is East Saint Georges Avenue today, Henry is East Henry Street and Blancke is East Blancke Street.
Hackensack Avenue, between Passaic and Monmouth Avenues, has no counterpart in today's street data.
Union Avenue has no junction with the streets of this part in today's data; not used for control.
Block 240 on St. George Avenue is marked 400 feet not in scale.
Public School No. 4 on block 267.

sheet-6-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 6 shows Grasselli Park, the company housing development of the Grasselli Chemical Company at Tremley in the south of Linden, drawn west of the heavy dividing line and at its own angle to the page. Lower Road to Rahway runs along the top and Tremley Point Road down the eastern side of the part, beside the dividing line; Parkway runs along the western side. Between them Buchanan, Madison and Monroe Streets cross the park to Grasselli Avenue, and Hayes runs in a curve below Monroe. South of these, Main, Arthur, Irene and Walter Streets run from the western margin to Tremley Point Road, crossed by Eldor Avenue, and Wood Avenue enters diagonally from the east to meet Tremley Point Road. The Jersey Shore Line Railroad, the electric line of the Public Service Corporation, crosses the lower part, and beyond it on Private Street stand the dining room, dormitories and laundry of the Grasselli Chemical Company camp on block 449. The houses of the park are rows of small one- and two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots, many with garages; a community house with auditorium and gymnasium, built of hollow cement block and drawn from plans, stands at Parkway and Hayes, and there are a chapel on block 453 and a dispensary and office on Grasselli Avenue. On Tremley Point Road and Wood Avenue are stores, saloons, a barber, a meat and grocery store and the house of the Lincoln Volunteer Hose Company of the fire department. A small stream and a wooden bridge appear at the upper left. Block numbers run from 448 to 455 and 540 to 545, with 141. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Parkway is Parkway Avenue today; Buchanan, Madison, Monroe, Main, Arthur, Irene and Walter are Buchanan, Madison, Monroe, Main, Arthur, Irene and Walter Streets; Hayes is Hayes Avenue; Lower Road to Rahway is Lower Road; Wood Avenue is South Wood Avenue.
Eldor Avenue is not in today's street data.
Grasselli Chemical Company camp with dining room, dormitories and laundry; community house with auditorium and gymnasium drawn from plans.
The part is drawn turned against part 1 of the sheet (fitted rotation about 74 degrees against 51).

sheet-7-1.description: The western part of sheet 7 covers the residential blocks between Henry Street and Elizabeth Avenue on the west side of the Borough of Linden, divided from the eastern part of the sheet by a heavy vertical line. Laurita, Miltonia, Dewitt and Lafayette Streets run up the page, crossed by Henry, Elm and Knopf Streets; Blancke Street and Stiles Street cut diagonally across the lower half, and a short street lettered Not Named runs between Blancke Street and Elizabeth Avenue beside Lindegar Street at the western margin. Donaldson Place runs along the eastern edge below Blancke Street. The blocks are laid out in narrow building lots with scattered small frame dwellings, a number of them hollow tile and stuccoed, and private garages; much of the area is still vacant. The one industrial plant is the Transatlantic Chemical Corporation, makers of coal tar intermediates, on block 88 south of Elizabeth Avenue, a fireproof reinforced concrete and brick plant built in 1920 with manufacturing, pipe shop, storage and laboratory buildings, fuel oil and toluol tanks and a siding beside the railroad, which crosses the bottom of the sheet. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in most of the streets and a 36-inch pipe crosses the lower part of the sheet. Block numbers include 26, 32 to 34, 45 to 48, 60, 63 to 68, 85, 88 and 551. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 50 degrees to the page; the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Henry, Elm, Blancke and Elizabeth Avenue are West Henry Street, West Elm Street, West Blancke Street and West Elizabeth Avenue today; Stiles is North Stiles Street.
The street lettered Not Named between Blancke Street and Elizabeth Avenue was not identified and was not used for control.
Transatlantic Chemical Corporation plant, built 1920, coal tar intermediates.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a vertical heavy line: left, Laurita, Miltonia, Dewitt, Lafayette x Henry, Elm, Knopf, Blancke, Stiles, Elizabeth (part 1); right, Wood Av, 10th to 18th St, Clinton, Edgar Rd, brook (part 2).

sheet-7-2.description: The eastern part of sheet 7 covers the numbered streets of Linden south of Edgar Road, on both sides of Wood Avenue, divided from the western part of the sheet by a heavy vertical line. Wood Avenue runs up the middle of the part from Edgar Road at the top to 18th Street at the bottom edge, and Clinton Street runs along the eastern margin. The cross streets are 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th, 17th and 18th Streets; 12th and 13th Streets are drawn only east of Wood Avenue, where block 380 west of the avenue is still unplatted, and Wood Place is lettered just north of Edgar Road. West Brook crosses the part diagonally from the north arrow near the dividing line to the eastern edge, passing under Wood Avenue at 14th Street. The blocks are divided into narrow lots and are partly built up with small frame dwellings, many with stores in front along Wood Avenue: groceries, a hardware and confectionery store, a tailor, a cobbler, a meat market, a fruit store, a barber and an office. A synagogue stands on block 148 near 18th Street, and Linden Public School No. 2, a large brick building with reinforced concrete floors in the corridors, occupies the front of block 143 at Wood Avenue and 17th Street. A two-storey building of flats with a grocery stands at Edgar Road and Wood Avenue, and a saloon at the eastern end of Edgar Road. A ten-inch water pipe is drawn in Wood Avenue. Block numbers run from 117 to 148, with 380. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: The numbered streets are East and West 10th to 18th Street today (East of Wood Avenue, West of it), and Wood Avenue is South Wood Avenue; Edgar Road is East Edgar Road.
18th Street lies on the bottom edge of the part; its junction with Wood Avenue was rejected by the fit (17 m).
Linden Public School No. 2 and a synagogue on block 148.

100 ft. Two parts divided by a vertical heavy line: left, Laurita, Miltonia, Dewitt, Lafayette x Henry, Elm, Knopf, Blancke, Stiles, Elizabeth (part 1); right, Wood Av, 10th to 18th St, Clinton, Edgar Rd, brook (part 2).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the central part of the Borough of Linden from Elm Street at the top to Linden Avenue at the bottom, and from Lafayette Street at the left to Wood Avenue, which runs diagonally near the right-hand edge. It is the sheet below sheet 2 and sheet 3, and the Pennsylvania Railroad crosses it near the bottom. Four rows of blocks between Elm Street, Knopf Street and Blancke Street, numbered 38 to 44 and 54 to 60, lie in the upper half; Spruce Street, Miner Terrace, Brook Street, Ainsworth Street and Helen Street run through them. They are cut into narrow lots, with scattered frame dwellings, many of hollow tile and stucco. West Brook winds down through the sheet from Elm Street, crosses Blancke Street, and continues south past the lumber yard to the bottom edge. Blancke Street runs obliquely across the sheet. Below it, Price Street and Elizabeth Avenue run east and west, with Donaldson Place and Lumber Street between them. The Linden Coal, Lumber and Building Supply Corporation yard stands between Elizabeth Avenue and the railroad. Near the right edge, between Blancke Street and Wood Avenue, stand a Methodist Episcopal church, the Linden Borough Hall with the fire department and post office, and a row of shops. The Pennsylvania Railroad is drawn as a wide band of tracks, with the freight depot, waiting room and coal pocket beside it and the passenger depot at the right. Jefferson Avenue and Penn Place run south from the railroad to Linden Avenue, with blocks 78 to 80. Stiles Street, with a 36-inch water pipe, runs diagonally at the lower left. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with a compass rose and graphic scale near the bottom left.
notes: Elm and Blancke are West Elm Street and West Blancke Street today; Donaldson Place keeps its name and Elizabeth Avenue is West Elizabeth Avenue.
Price Street, as drawn in the middle of the sheet, is not in today's street data near here.
Stiles Street is not in today's street data.
Brook Street at Blancke Street was rejected as a control point by 6.5 m: the brook and the street bend there.
100 ft. Wood Av, Elizabeth, Blancke, Price, Lumber, Penn RR, brook; one part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the southeast part of the central Borough of Linden, from Blancke Street at the top to Morris Avenue at the bottom, and from Wood Avenue at the left to the east side of Maple Avenue and Cartaret Street. Washington Avenue meets Blancke Street at the top left. Blancke Street runs obliquely across the upper left and then straight along the top, with Hussa Street, Price Street and Elizabeth Avenue crossing the sheet below it in long rows of narrow lots, numbered 50, 51, 55, 62 and 65. St. Elizabeth Roman Catholic Church and its rectory stand on Blancke Street, and a row of shops, a motion picture theatre, a bank and the Linden Manufacturing Company's underwear works stand along Wood Avenue at the left edge. Todd Place, Maple Avenue and Ziegler Avenue, drawn diagonally, break up the right side of the sheet. Across the middle runs the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn as a wide band of tracks with a viaduct at Wood Avenue, and Pennsylvania Avenue runs along it on the north side. South of the tracks Pennsylvania Railroad Avenue, Linden Avenue and Morris Avenue are crossed by Clinton Street and Cartaret Street, with blocks numbered 70 to 75, 83 and 87 to 88. The Linden Hotel stands on Wood Avenue, and the Krayer Chemical Company works, marked as now vacant, stands north of Linden Avenue. A Borough line runs through the lower blocks, and a small brook crosses the bottom right near Woodlawn Avenue. A cemetery occupies the lower right corner, with the lodge beyond the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with a compass rose and a graphic scale.
notes: Blancke is East Blancke Street today; Elizabeth Avenue, Linden Avenue and Morris Avenue are East Elizabeth Avenue, East Linden Avenue and East Morris Avenue east of Wood Avenue.
Penna. Railroad Avenue is printed with Penna. for Pennsylvania; the street keeps that name today.
Cartaret is Carteret Street today.
Todd Place is Todd Street today.
Price Street is not in today's street data near here, and Price Street was not used for control.
100 ft. Blancke, Elizabeth, Penna Railroad Av, Linden Av, Morris Av, Penn RR; one part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the residential grid in the middle of the Borough of Linden, between Henry Street at the top and Pennsylvania Avenue at the bottom, and from Pratt Place at the left to Lincoln Street at the right. The streets are laid out as a regular grid: Roselle Street, Harrison Place, Bower Street, McCandless Street and Lincoln Street run down the sheet, and Henry, Elm, Passaic, Hackensack, Monmouth, Blancke, Hussa, Bergen, Essex, Elizabeth and Pennsylvania cross them, with the blocks numbered 47 to 73, 243 to 248, 271 to 277 and 302 to 307. Almost all the blocks are cut into narrow building lots, and in the right-hand half of the sheet most are still vacant. Houses are scattered through the older blocks on the left, nearly all small frame dwellings, some stuccoed, with a few private garages. Ziegler Avenue cuts diagonally across the middle of the sheet from lower left to upper right and breaks the regular blocks into wedges, and the compass rose is drawn in the angle of Ziegler Avenue and the blocks beside it. The larger buildings are a synagogue and a few stores near Blancke Street, a pink-tinted building on Ziegler Avenue at Roselle Street, and a fire alarm box at Elizabeth Avenue and Roselle Street. The Pennsylvania Railroad is drawn along the bottom edge. Sheet 3 lies to the west. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 51 degrees on the page, and a title cartouche and scale note are placed in the vacant blocks at the top right.
notes: Henry, Elm, Blancke and Elizabeth Avenue are East Henry Street, East Elm Street, East Blancke Street and East Elizabeth Avenue today.
Hackensack Avenue and Monmouth Place are not in today's street data; Monmouth Avenue is used for the Monmouth Place and Monmouth Avenue rows.
Lincoln Street at Pennsylvania Avenue was rejected as a control point by 9.7 m.
The Pennsylvania Railroad drawn along the bottom edge is the line now called the Northeast Corridor.
100 ft. Henry, Elm, Monmouth Pl, Blancke, Hussa, Bergen, Elizabeth, Pennsylvania Av, Ziegler, Roselle; one part.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 covers central Linden south of Linden Avenue, on both sides of Wood Avenue, down to Edgar Road. Linden Avenue runs along the top, with the old borough line drawn across the first row of blocks; below it Morris Avenue, Munsell Avenue, Stimson Avenue, Cedar Avenue, Union Avenue and Liberty Avenue cross the eastern half, and Jefferson Avenue, Penn Place, Clark and Mitchell Avenue run down the western half. Wood Avenue crosses the part from top to bottom, with Wood Place branching off it below Union Avenue, and Clinton Street and Woodlawn Avenue run down the east side. In the southwest Stimson Street cuts diagonally across, and Bogert and Corbet are short streets between Clark and the west margin; West Creek and a branch of the brook wind through this corner and under Wood Avenue near Munsell Avenue. The blocks near Linden and Wood Avenues hold stores and public buildings: groceries, a meat market, tenements, a harness shop, a pool room, a garage with auto supplies, a bakery, the Fire Department's Engine Company No. 1 on Morris Avenue, Linden Town Hall on Wood Avenue and the Progress Club near Mitchell Avenue. Elsewhere the lots carry scattered frame dwellings, many stuccoed, with stables, sheds and a blacksmith shop; block 85 between Wood Avenue and the brook is largely open, and block 95 in the lower left is left blank here because it is drawn in the inset below. Block numbers run from 75 to 111. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with water pipes of 6 to 36 inches shown in the streets.
notes: Linden Avenue, Morris Avenue and Munsell Avenue are East and West Linden, Morris and Munsell Avenue today (east and west of Wood Avenue); Wood Avenue is South Wood Avenue; Liberty Avenue is Liberty Street; Edgar Road is East Edgar Road.
Stimson Avenue, Stimson Street, Bogert and Corbet are not in today's street data.
Linden Town Hall on Wood Avenue; Fire Department Engine Company No. 1 on Morris Avenue.
Block 95 (W.J. Bush and Co. chemical works) is drawn in the 50 ft inset in the lower left of the sheet, which was not placed.

100 ft main part (Linden Av, Morris, Munsell, Stimson, Cedar, Union, Liberty, Edgar Rd, Jefferson, Penn Pl, Clark, Mitchell, Wood, Clinton, Woodlawn); 50 ft inset bottom left: W.J. Bush & Co chemical works on Stimson (part 2). Part 2 not placed (no street junction).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset (50 ft): W.J. Bush & Co. chemical works, block 95 on Stimson Street (no street junction; Stimson Street is not in today's data and the main part leaves block 95 blank; needs step 6b: parcel-corner control).

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 12 shows a small residential tract on the east side of Edgar Road in the northeast of Linden, next to the area of sheet 13, separated from the industrial part below by a heavy line along which is lettered Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey beyond, Bay Way Refinery. Edgar Road runs diagonally along the western side; Grier Avenue runs down the middle from Malcolm Place at the top, crossed by Louis Avenue, Tuxedo Place and Ida Avenue, and Willard Place and Bedle Place bound the tract to the south and east, with the short Klem Avenue in the upper right. West of Grier Avenue, Oak Place and Elm Place are short streets running off Edgar Road. The blocks are cut into narrow lots, many of them still vacant, with scattered small frame dwellings, a few stores and garages; block 552 south of Willard Place is open land. Block numbers run from 403 to 416 and 552. A heavy line along the east side of Bedle Place separates this part from the numbered streets of part 3. sheet-12-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 12 continues the numbered streets of south Linden beyond sheet 7, on both sides of Wood Avenue, turned on the page so that Wood Avenue runs across it and the north arrow points to the upper left. Clinton Street, lettered Clinton St. or Roll Av. and drawn 100 feet wide, runs across the top, Wood Avenue across the middle and Winans Avenue below it; 18th, 19th and 20th Streets run down the page between them. Forty Acre Road cuts diagonally across the lower right corner to the heavy line that separates this part from the inset below, and West Brook loops in at the top edge. The blocks are divided into narrow lots and partly built up with small frame dwellings, many stuccoed, with a few brick houses, a grocery and notions store, a dry goods and confectionery store, a tobacco and sporting goods store, a junk shop and garages; blocks 159 and parts of 167 and 171 to the east are open. A 12-inch water pipe runs in Forty Acre Road and 20th Street and 6- and 10-inch pipes in the other streets. Block numbers run from 144 to 171 and 383 to 385. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the northeast corner of the Borough of Linden, along the city line with Elizabeth. The line is drawn along the top of the sheet with the words City of Elizabeth, and Allen is the first street below it. Edgar Road, drawn as a slanting line at the left, bounds the sheet on the west, and a strip of open ground labelled for a Standard Oil Company refinery lies off the east edge. The streets are laid out in a grid turned about 42 degrees counterclockwise from the page, so that north points to the upper left, unlike the sheets to the west. Grier Avenue, Klem Avenue and Bedle Place run down the sheet, crossed by Allen, Meacham Avenue, Bacheller Avenue, Dennis Place, McGilvary Place, McCandless Place, Shawell Avenue, Titsworth Avenue, Mack Place, Gilchrist Avenue and Malcolm Place, with Von Spiegel Place near the west side. The blocks, numbered 408 to 446, are mostly cut into narrow building lots, closely built up with small frame dwellings in the northwest, and thinner toward the east and south. Public School No. 3, a brick building with classrooms alongside, stands on the block between Bacheller Avenue and Dennis Place, and the Washington Volunteer Hose Company house stands on Dennis Place. The Grier Avenue Methodist Episcopal Church stands on Grier Avenue north of Titsworth Avenue, and a club house stands near Shawell Avenue. A small stream with a bridge crosses the lower blocks, passing under Von Spiegel Place and Titsworth Avenue. A wedge of vacant ground cut by a street labelled Not Named separates the left-hand blocks from Edgar Road, and a second Not Named street lies east of Klem Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with a compass rose and graphic scale at the right and bottom, and sheet 12 lies to the south.
notes: Edgar Road is East Edgar Road (US 1) today, widened since 1920; it was not used for control.
Bedle Place and its junctions were not used for control: the street is platted differently today.
McGilvary Place, Shawell Avenue and Titsworth Avenue are not in today's street data.
Two streets are labelled Not Named on the sheet.
The sheet is turned: north points to the upper left, at about -42 degrees.
